card.name: Judgment-of-the-physician and benefit-risk phrases
card.fires_on: Small words inside caveat clauses such as "unless in the judgment <<of>> the physician" or "unless the benefits <<clearly>> outweigh the risks". Also fires on "only" in "only if clearly needed" and on "consultation" after "consider".

modes.label: Judgment of the physician
modes.description: The word "of" right after "in the judgment" or "in the opinion" in a unless-clause.
modes.example: unless in the judgment<< of>> the physician the potential benefits of treatment outweigh

modes.label: Benefits clearly outweigh
modes.description: Words like "clearly" or "only" in a conditional clause about benefits outweighing risks or being clearly needed.
modes.example: unless the benefits<< clearly>> outweigh the risks.

modes.label: Consider consultation
modes.description: The word "consultation" after "consider" when advising referral to a specialist.
modes.example: consider<< consultation>> with an allergist-immunologist prior

card.writes: It adds a slight push toward words like "custom" and "customize", which suggests individualized decisions, but the effect is weak.
card.plain: It marks the hedging phrases that leave a treatment choice to the clinician's judgment of individual benefit and risk.
